record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; the paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README and file list describe refusal-direction projection and ablation code/data, but report no result testing whether the direction causes refusal or whether attacks suppress it.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal outcomes for attacks, but no result about the direction itself. Those outcomes are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions; file names alone do not establish that a direction intervention ran or worked.
record.test_reason: The repo's title asks how quantization changes refusal-direction suppression across turns, and it contains direction, ablation and projection code and data. The README, the only text read, reports no direction-level result. It gives only refusal and harm rates under attacks, so no version can be judged from the available text.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors found 4-bit quantization does not weaken multi-turn jailbreak resistance overall. Their headline is that non-refusal scoring ranks CoSafe above Crescendo while attributable harm reverses this (+4.9pp, CI excluding zero across judges and labelling rules). Adaptive-attack quantization effects average 8.1pp vs 1.6pp for static attacks, against a 0.5pp FP16 backend control.
record.recipe_differences: The repository investigates quantization, multi-turn attacks, refusal scoring, and harm attribution. It does not report using the original difference-in-means direction intervention as a tested method. Research repository with code and data, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports differences by model family and attack type, and says quantization effects differ between adaptive and static attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen2.5 refuses 99% of single-turn harmful prompts but 7.5% under multi-turn attack. Llama-3.x hardens against escalation. Mistral-7B barely refuses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-turn refusal robustness varies by model family and is not predicted by single-turn refusal rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-refusal success rates rank CoSafe above Crescendo (81.9% vs 20.2%), while attack-attributable harm reverses the order (1.1% vs 6.0%). Reversal +4.9pp, 95% CI [+1.9, +8.2].
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-based jailbreak success metrics can misrank attacks relative to attributable harm.

record.problems: The repository text is limited to README and file-list metadata; code and the full write-up were not read or run. The README says human validation on a 200-row stratified sample remains open and a clean fully-adaptive PAIR rerun is outstanding.
record.rows_left_out: No direction-specific results are reported in the README. Other summary results about harm attribution and attack-ranking inversion do not measure a claim version's direction or refusal effect.

untested.parts: No reported ablation or addition effect on refusal, and no capability check. ablation.py exists but no results are reported.
No reported projection or suppression trajectory of the direction under multi-turn attacks. No adversarial-training result.
Refusal is contrasted with harm only behaviourally, via output judges. No representational separation of harm and refusal is tested.
No cross-precision, cross-language or base-to-instruct direction-transfer result is reported.

missing.what: Per-turn projection of activations onto the refusal direction across attack arms and precisions (multi-turn suppression trajectory). This could bear on V3, whether attacks suppress the direction, and on V6 across quantized variants.
missing.locator: paper/main.tex; data/incontext/incontext_*.csv ('refusal + projection per arm'); src/multiturn_projection.py

missing.what: Results of the direction ablation / causal-layer experiment, if reported.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available. The repository's stated question concerns refusal-direction suppression trajectories, so the paper and the incontext CSVs may contain V3-relevant projection results. A full read of paper/main.tex is needed before the T4 classification can be trusted.

versions.untested_parts: Difference-in-means direction, causal ablation/addition effects, and preservation of other abilities.
No released-model weight edit or resulting refusal behavior is reported.
Attack outcomes are reported, but no result tests whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No comparison of harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct direction-transfer result.
No result testing how refusal-training choices determine direction removability.
